_schema: Each entry creates one QUOTES edge (nt_ref → ot_ref). Block quotes use anchor verses on both sides; full range documented in notes.

quotes.notes: Virgin birth. LXX παρθένος (virgin) renders Heb עַלְמָה (young woman of marriageable age); the 'sign' hinges on the LXX specificity.
Bethlehem prophecy. Matthew's wording rearranges MT; 'by no means least' inverts Micah's 'small among the clans'.
Typological reading. Hosea's original referent is corporate Israel at the Exodus; Matthew applies it to Messiah as true Israel.
Rachel weeping for her children — originally the Babylonian exile; Matthew applies to Herod's massacre.
Voice in the wilderness. John the Baptist's identification.
Temptation #1 response. 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'
Satan's quotation. Cites Psa 91:11-12 to tempt Jesus — shows Scripture can be weaponized out of context.
Temptation #2 response. 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'
Temptation #3 response. 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.'
Galilee of the Gentiles (Isa 9:1-2). Anchor NT Matt 4:15; quote extends through 4:16.
Messenger who prepares the way — applied to John the Baptist.
Hardening prophecy (Isa 6:9-10). Why Jesus speaks in parables.
Fifth commandment, cited against corban tradition.
Honor with lips; heart far from me.
Male and female he created them. Jesus grounds marriage in creation.
One flesh. Paired with Matt 19:4 quoting Gen 1:27 — two OT sources in one argument.
King on a donkey. Triumphal entry fulfillment.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Crowd's acclaim.
Temple cleansing. 'My house shall be called a house of prayer.'
Second half of Matt 21:13: 'den of robbers' — conflated quotation with Isa 56:7.
Stone the builders rejected — cornerstone (118:22-23).
God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob — resurrection argument from the present-tense verb.
Greatest commandment — the Shema's second half.
Love your neighbor — second greatest commandment.
The Lord said to my Lord — Christological argument to silence Pharisees.
Strike the shepherd, sheep scattered — predicted at Last Supper.
30 pieces of silver (Zech 11:12-13). Matthew attributes to Jeremiah — classic exegetical puzzle; may be conflation with Jer 19:1-13 or 32:6-9.
Eli Eli lama sabachthani. Aramaic transliteration of the Hebrew. Lamp uses Heb versification: Psa 22:1 (superscription) → Eng Psa 22:0, so Heb 22:2 = Eng 22:1.
Messenger prep. Mark attributes the composite Mal 3:1 + Isa 40:3 to 'Isaiah' — similar attribution flattening.
Voice in the wilderness — paired with Mark 1:2 citing Mal 3:1.
Shema prefix. Mark preserves 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord' — Matthew omits v. 4.
Nazareth synagogue reading (Isa 61:1-2). Jesus stops mid-sentence before 'day of vengeance' — a hermeneutical statement.
Into your hands I commit my spirit. Jesus' final words in Luke. Heb 31:6 = Eng 31:5.
Zeal for your house. Disciples remember this at temple cleansing. Heb 69:10 = Eng 69:9.
Bread from heaven. Conflates with Exo 16:4/15.
I said, you are gods. Jesus' defense of his 'Son of God' claim from Psa 82.
Donkey prophecy — John's distinct citation vs Matt 21:5.
Who has believed our report? John's explanation for unbelief.
Blinded eyes, hardened hearts — John cites after explicit reference to Isaiah 'seeing his glory' (12:41).
Lifted up his heel against me. Jesus applies to Judas at Last Supper. Heb 41:10 = Eng 41:9.
Hated me without cause — Jesus cites 'their law' (Psalms counted as Torah). Heb 69:5 = Eng 69:4.
Divided my garments. Passion fulfillment. Heb 22:19 = Eng 22:18 (superscription offset).
Not a bone broken — Passover lamb regulation applied to Jesus; possibly conflated with Psa 34:20.
They shall look on him whom they have pierced.
Peter applies to Judas: 'Let his habitation be desolate.' Heb 69:26 = Eng 69:25.
Second half of Peter's Judas argument: 'Let another take his office.'
Pentecost. Peter quotes Joel 3:1-5 Heb (2:28-32 Eng); 'last days' replaces Joel's 'afterward'. Lamp uses Hebrew versification.
David's foresight of resurrection (Heb Psa 16:9-12 = Eng 16:8-11). Peter: David speaks of the Messiah.
Sit at my right hand — Peter's ascension argument.
Kings of the earth set themselves (Psa 2:1-2). Applied to Pilate/Herod/Gentiles/Israel.
Stephen: heaven is my throne — argument against temple-centrism before the Sanhedrin.
Ethiopian eunuch's passage — Philip interprets Isa 53:7-8 Christologically.
You are my son, today I have begotten you — applied to resurrection in Paul's Antioch sermon.

James at Jerusalem Council: Amos 9:11-12 (LXX). LXX 'that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord' differs from MT 'that they may possess the remnant of Edom' — the LXX reading is what grounds the Gentile-inclusion argument.
The just shall live by faith — Reformation keystone; also cited at Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:38.
None righteous — opening of Rom 3:10-18 catena quoting Psa 14:1-3 Eng (Heb 14:2-4; also parallel Psa 53:1-3 Eng).
Throat an open grave. Second item in Rom 3 catena; conflated with Psa 140:3. Heb 5:10 = Eng 5:9.
Mouth full of cursing. Third item in Rom 3 catena.
Feet swift to shed blood (Isa 59:7-8). Fourth item in Rom 3 catena.
No fear of God. Final item in Rom 3 catena. Heb 36:2 = Eng 36:1.
Abraham believed God — keystone for justification by faith; also at Gal 3:6 and Jas 2:23.
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven (Psa 32:1-2 Eng / Heb 32:2-3). David's witness to imputed righteousness.
Jacob I loved, Esau I hated — Mal 1:2-3; central to election argument.
I will have mercy on whom I have mercy — divine freedom in election.
The man who does them shall live by them — Paul's foil to faith-righteousness.
Word is near you — Paul Christologizes Deut 30:12-14.
Whoever calls on the name of the Lord — identifies 'the Lord' (YHWH) with Jesus. Heb Joel 3:5 = Eng Joel 2:32.
Their table a snare (Eng 69:22-23 / Heb 69:23-24) — applied to Israel's hardening.
Vengeance is mine — grounds pacifist ethic in divine justice.
Burning coals — enemy-feeding ethic from Proverbs.
Root of Jesse — Gentile hope grounded in Davidic covenant.
Destroy the wisdom of the wise.
Eye has not seen — Paul's source debated (possibly combined Isa 64:4 + Isa 65:17; some think apocryphal source).
One flesh — applied to illicit unions.
Do not muzzle the ox — Paul reads typologically to argue for apostolic support.
Golden calf: people sat down to eat and rose up to play.
All things under his feet. Heb 8:7 = Eng 8:6.
First Adam became a living soul — typological Adam/Christ.
Death swallowed up in victory.
O death, where is your sting.
Manna gathering — neither lack nor surplus; applied to giving.
Abraham believed God — Galatians' keystone.
In you shall all nations be blessed — 'preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham'.
Cursed is everyone who does not abide by all things — Paul's argument that law-keeping is totalizing.
The just shall live by faith — second Pauline citation; also at Rom 1:17.
Cursed is everyone hanged on a tree — applied to crucifixion.
Rejoice, O barren — Sarah/Jerusalem above allegory.
Cast out the slave woman — Hagar/Ishmael applied to Sinai covenant.
Love neighbor — whole law fulfilled in this word.
Ascended on high, led captivity captive. Paul's form differs from both MT and LXX — possibly from a targum tradition. Heb 68:19 = Eng 68:18.
One flesh — applied to Christ and church.
Honor your father and mother — 'first commandment with a promise'.
You are my son — first of Hebrews 1 catena; Davidic enthronement Psalm applied to Christ's exaltation.
I will be to him a father — second clause of Heb 1:5, Davidic covenant.
Let all the angels of God worship him — LXX reading absent from MT but attested in 4QDeutq (Dead Sea Scrolls).
Makes his angels spirits — Hebrews reads Psa 104:4 as angels-subordination to the Son.
Your throne, O God (Eng 45:6-7 / Heb 45:7-8) — royal wedding psalm applied to Son's divinity.
Loved righteousness, hated wickedness; God has anointed you — continuation of Heb 1:8 (Psa 45:7-8 Heb / 45:6-7 Eng); the 'God, your God' phrase grounds the Son-vs-Father address.
You, Lord, laid the foundations of the earth (Eng 102:25-27 / Heb 102:26-28) — cosmological psalm applied to Son.
Sit at my right hand — closing citation of Hebrews 1 catena.
What is man (Eng Psa 8:4-6 / Heb 8:5-7). LXX 'angels' for MT Elohim — grounds the 'lower than angels' argument.
Made him a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory — continuation of Heb 2:6. Heb 8:6 = Eng 8:5.

Put all things in subjection under his feet — third quote from Psa 8 in three verses; the author then exegetes 'all things' (οὐδὲν ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ ἀνυπότακτον) to mean nothing is excluded, yet 'we do not yet see' it fulfilled except in Jesus. Heb 8:7 = Eng 8:6.
I will declare your name to my brothers — Christ on the lips of the Davidic sufferer (Psa 22). Lament-to-praise turn applied to the resurrection congregation. Heb 22:23 = Eng 22:22.
I will put my trust in him — first of two Isa 8 citations in Heb 2:13. Hebrews puts Isaiah's confession on Christ's lips.
Behold I and the children God has given me — second OT citation in same NT verse, immediately following Isa 8:17. The 'children' typologically the believers Christ identifies with.
Today if you hear his voice (Psa 95:7-11). Wilderness generation as warning.
As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my rest — closes the Psa 95:7-11 block begun at Heb 3:7. The whole Heb 3:7-11 quotation runs Psa 95:7b-11.
Today if you hear his voice — re-quote of Heb 3:7 anchor as the author drives the warning home.
Re-quote of 'they shall not enter my rest' — used now to derive a Sabbath-rest theology distinct from the wilderness rest.
Third quotation of Psa 95:11 in two chapters — emphasis on the unfulfilled remainder of the rest promise.
Today if you hear his voice — re-quote attributed 'through David' to separate the rest promise from Joshua's conquest (which would have made the promise obsolete).

You are my Son, today I have begotten you — applied to the high-priestly calling (Christ did not glorify himself). Same verse Paul cites at Acts 13:33 for resurrection; Hebrews redirects it to priesthood.
You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek — foundation of Hebrews' priesthood argument.

Surely blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you — the Abrahamic oath at the Aqedah cited as the paradigm of God's irrevocable promise; the doubled verb preserves Hebrew waw-emphatic.
Second citation of Psa 110:4 (after Heb 5:6) — now anchoring the entire Melchizedek typology of Heb 7.
Third Psa 110:4 quote. Emphasis on the oath formula ('the Lord has sworn and will not relent') as the unique mark of this priesthood vs the Levitical (which was sworn-free).
See that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain — foundation of Hebrews' tabernacle typology (earthly sanctuary as shadow of heavenly).
New covenant (Jer 31:31-34). Longest OT quotation in NT; grounds obsolescence argument for old covenant.

This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded for you — Hebrews substitutes 'God commanded' (LXX-like) for MT 'YHWH has cut with you'. Cited at the institution of the new covenant; same wording also echoes the eucharist formulas.
A body you have prepared for me — LXX σῶμα for MT 'ears you have opened' (אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ). The LXX reading is load-bearing for Hebrews' incarnation/sacrifice argument. Heb 40:7 = Eng 40:6.

Then I said, behold I come... to do your will, O God — continuation of Heb 10:5 (Psa 40:7-9). The 'I come to do your will' is the hinge between sacrifice replacement and Christ's obedience. Heb 40:8 = Eng 40:7.
I will put my laws on their hearts — re-quote of the new-covenant promise (anchor at Heb 8:8/Jer 31:31), now after the 'one offering' argument and in condensed form.
I will remember their sins no more — cap of the new-covenant re-quote, used to argue that ongoing sacrifices are now unnecessary.
Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord — cited as warning to apostates. Same verse Paul cites at Rom 12:19 with the opposite force (don't take vengeance yourself).
He who is coming will come — opens the composite Hab 2:3-4 quote.
The just shall live by faith — Hab 2:4 cited third time in NT (also Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11).

Enoch was taken so that he should not see death — Hebrews uses LXX μετετέθη (transferred/translated); MT 'he was not, for God took him' is more elliptical and would not by itself yield 'did not see death'.
Through Isaac shall your offspring be named — foundation of the resurrection-faith argument: God promised the line through the very son Abraham was asked to sacrifice (Heb 11:19).
My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord (Prov 3:11-12).

Whom the Lord loves he chastens — continuation of Heb 12:5. Hebrews follows LXX 'scourges every son he receives' (μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται); MT reads 'as a father the son in whom he delights' (וּכְאָב אֶת־בֵּן יִרְצֶה).

Moses said: I tremble with fear — Hebrews dramatizes Sinai by attributing to that scene Moses' confession from Deu 9:19, where the terror was actually over the golden calf. Hermeneutically, both are theophanic-judgment moments.

Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens — eschatological citation. The 'once more' (ἔτι ἅπαξ) is what the author exegetes to mean the final removal of created shakable things.
For our God is a consuming fire — Sinai-language applied to the eschatological judgment, paired with the Hag 2:6 citation at Heb 12:26.
I will never leave you — Deut 31:6/Josh 1:5 (nearly identical phrasing in both).
The Lord is my helper; I will not fear — answer to the love-of-money command at Heb 13:5.
Love neighbor — 'royal law'.
Abraham believed God — James's use alongside Rom 4:3 generates the faith/works tension.
Be holy, for I am holy — Levitical holiness code applied to Christians.
Behold, I am laying in Zion a cornerstone — Messianic stone.
Stone the builders rejected — same OT verse as Matt 21:42.
No deceit in his mouth — Suffering Servant applied to Christ's sinlessness.
By his wounds you have been healed — Isa 53:4-5.
God opposes the proud — also cited at Jas 4:6.
